title: PDP 1321/2024: consent must be free, informed, specific, clear and active
claim: The Ethiopian Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 requires that consent of a data subject be free, informed, specific, clear and given through an active action, and permits withdrawal of consent at any time.
evidence_summary: Article 8 of Proclamation No. 1321/2024 sets out the conditions for valid consent: personal data may be processed on the basis of consent given before processing commences; for consent to be valid it must be free, informed, specific, clear and require an active action; and the data subject may withdraw consent at any time.
source_excerpt: 8. Conditions for Consent 1/ For the purpose of Article 7 Sub-Article (2) lit. (a) Of this Proclamation, personal data should be processed on the basis of the consent given prior to the commencement of the processing. 2/ For the consent of the data subject to be valid, it must be free, informed, specific, clear and require an active action from the data subject. 3/ The data subject may withdraw his consent at any time.
interpretation: Normative evidence of the legal consent standard in Ethiopia's 2024 data protection law. The standard is consent-opt-in: valid consent requires an active action and cannot be passive. This establishes what the law requires, not how consent is obtained in practice.
citation: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, Art. 8(1)-(3) (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 35, 24 July 2024).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (Article 8).
keywords: consent, data protection, Ethiopia, personal data
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/1/eth_pdp_1321.pdf); locator Article 8.

title: PDP 1321/2024: data localization requirement for Ethiopian servers
claim: The Ethiopian Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 requires that personal data collected or obtained locally be stored on a server or data center located in Ethiopia, and requires prior Authority approval for cross-border transfer of sensitive personal data.
evidence_summary: Article 22 ('Data Sovereignty') requires every data controller or data processor to store personal data collected or obtained locally on a server or data center in Ethiopia; permits the Authority to designate categories of critical personal data that may only be processed in Ethiopia; and requires prior approval for cross-border transfer of sensitive personal data.
source_excerpt: 22. Data Sovereignty 1/ Every data controller or data processor shall ensure the storage, on a server or data center located in Ethiopia, of personal data collected or obtained locally. 2/ The Authority shall prescribe, based on grounds of strategic interests of the state, categories of personal data as critical personal data that shall only be processed in a server or data center located in Ethiopia. 3/ Cross-border transfer of sensitive personal data shall require the prior approval of the Authority.
interpretation: Normative evidence of an explicit data-localization rule in Ethiopian law. This supports evidence that Ethiopia's 2024 data protection law adopts a territorial storage requirement and state-designated critical data categories. It does not by itself establish how the rule is enforced.
citation: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, Art. 22 (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 35, 24 July 2024).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (Article 22, Data Sovereignty).
keywords: data localization, sovereignty, cross-border transfer, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/1/eth_pdp_1321.pdf); locator Article 22.

title: PDP 1321/2024: data subject rights to information, access, erasure, objection, restriction and portability
claim: The Ethiopian Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 codifies a chapter of data subject rights including the right to be informed, right of access, right to erasure, right to object, restriction of processing and data portability.
evidence_summary: Chapter Three ('Rights of Data Subjects') of Proclamation No. 1321/2024 establishes rights including: the right to be provided information about processing (Art. 24), right of access free of charge (Art. 25), right to erasure (Art. 28), right to object (Art. 29), restriction of processing (Art. 30) and data portability (Art. 32).
source_excerpt: 25. Right of Access 1/ A data subject shall have a right to obtain, on request, at reasonable intervals, free of charge, and without excessive delay: a) Confirmation of the processing of personal data... 28. Right to Erasure 1/ A data subject shall have on request, free of charge and without excessive delay, the right to erasure of personal data where: a) The data are no longer necessary... 32. Right to Data Portability 1/ A data subject has the right to receive personal data concerning him... in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
interpretation: Normative evidence that Ethiopia's 2024 law formally recognizes a comprehensive set of individual data-subject rights. This establishes formal legal recognition; it does not evidence implementation or enforcement experience.
citation: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, Arts. 24, 25, 28, 29, 30, 32 (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 35, 24 July 2024).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quotes from primary legal text (Chapter Three, Rights of Data Subjects).
keywords: data subject rights, access, erasure, objection, portability, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/1/eth_pdp_1321.pdf); locators Articles 24-32.

title: PDP 1321/2024: Ethiopian Communications Authority as supervisory authority
claim: The Ethiopian Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the supervisory authority and gives it functions including maintaining a register of controllers, investigating complaints and cooperating with foreign authorities.
evidence_summary: Proclamation No. 1321/2024 defines 'Authority' as the Ethiopian Communications Authority established under Communications Proclamation No. 1148/2019, and assigns it supervisory functions including monitoring compliance, keeping a register of data controllers, investigating complaints and cooperating with supervisory authorities of other countries.
source_excerpt: 36/ 'Authority' means the Ethiopian Communications Authority established as per the Communications Proclamation No. 1148/2019... 9/ Cooperate with supervisory authorities of other countries; ... 11/ Investigate following legally established investigation procedures and principles complaints made to it... 12/ Keep and maintain Register of data controllers and data processors.
interpretation: Normative/institutional evidence that a designated supervisory authority exists under Ethiopian law as of 2024. This establishes the institutional mandate on paper; it does not evidence the authority's actual operational capacity or enforcement record.
citation: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, definition of 'Authority' and supervisory functions (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 35, 24 July 2024).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quotes from primary legal text (definitions and supervisory functions).
keywords: supervisory authority, Ethiopian Communications Authority, accountability, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/1/eth_pdp_1321.pdf).

title: PDP 1321/2024: right to lodge complaint with the Authority
claim: The Ethiopian Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 grants data subjects a right to submit complaints to the Authority for remedy of violations, and provides for administrative complaints against decisions.
evidence_summary: Article 58 of Proclamation No. 1321/2024 provides that data subjects may submit a written complaint to the Authority for remedy of violations of their rights, with further provisions on how complaints are processed.
source_excerpt: 58. Complaints 1/ Data subjects shall have the right to submit a complaint in writing to the Authority to have remedy for violation of his rights under this Proclamation.
interpretation: Normative evidence of a formal complaints/redress channel under the 2024 law. Establishes the legal right to complaint; does not evidence actual redress outcomes.
citation: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, Art. 58 (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 35, 24 July 2024).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (Article 58).
